text: Joseph fell upon his father's face, wept over him, and kissed him.

versions.text: Joseph threw himself on his father's face, wept over him, and kissed him.
versions.explanation: "Threw himself on his father's face" is an awkward collocation in English; "fell upon" renders וַיִּפֹּל plainly and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Then Joseph ordered the physicians in his service to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel.
It took forty days, for that is the full time required for embalming. And the Egyptians mourned him seventy days.
When the days of mourning were over, Joseph said to Pharaoh's household, "If I have found favor in your eyes, speak to Pharaoh on my behalf and say:
'My father made me swear an oath, saying, "I am about to die. Bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan." Now let me go up and bury my father, and then I will return.'"
Pharaoh answered, "Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear."
So Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went all Pharaoh's servants, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
along with all of Joseph's household, his brothers, and his father's household. Only their children, their flocks, and their herds were left behind in the land of Goshen.
Chariots and horsemen went up with him as well; it was a very great company.
When they came to the threshing floor of Atad, beyond the Jordan, they raised a great and solemn lament there, and Joseph observed seven days of mourning for his father.

versions.text: When they came to the threshing floor of Atad, beyond the Jordan, they raised a loud and bitter lament there, and Joseph observed seven days of mourning for his father.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew pairs גָּדוֹל (great) with כָבֵד מְאֹד (very heavy/weighty). The rendering "loud and bitter" loses the intensifier מְאֹד and shifts "heavy/solemn" to "bitter." "Great and solemn" keeps both terms and still reads smoothly aloud.

text: When the Canaanites who lived in the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a deep mourning for the Egyptians." That is why the place beyond the Jordan was named Abel Mizraim.[fn]

versions.text: When the Canaanites who lived in the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a solemn mourning of the Egyptians." That is why the place beyond the Jordan was named Abel Mizraim.
versions.explanation: כָּבֵד here means "heavy, deep" rather than "solemn," and the preposition לְ marks the Egyptians as the ones mourning ("for/of the Egyptians"). A footnote explaining that Abel Mizraim means "mourning of Egypt" would help the reader see the wordplay the verse depends on.

text: So Jacob's sons did for him just as he had commanded them:
they carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, the field near Mamre that Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
After burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, together with his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.
When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back in full for all the wrong we did to him?"
So they sent word to Joseph: "Before he died, your father gave this command:

'Say to Joseph: Please forgive your brothers' offense and their sin, the wrong they did you.' Now then, please forgive the offense of the servants of the God of your father." And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
Then his brothers came in person and fell down before him. "We are your slaves," they said.

versions.text: Then his brothers themselves came and threw themselves down before him. "We are your slaves," they said.
versions.explanation: The doubled "themselves ... threw themselves" is clumsy when read aloud. "Came in person" preserves the emphatic גַּם and "fell down" matches וַיִּפְּלוּ more directly.

text: But Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
You intended evil against me, but God intended it for good, to accomplish what is now being done: the saving of many lives.
So do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your children." And he comforted them and spoke kindly to them.
Joseph stayed in Egypt, he and his father's household, and he lived a hundred and ten years.

versions.text: Joseph stayed in Egypt, along with his father's household. He lived a hundred and ten years
versions.explanation: The verse ends without terminal punctuation and runs on grammatically into verse 23, which is confusing for a reader or listener hearing verses as units. Closing the sentence here keeps each verse self-contained.

text: He saw Ephraim's children to the third generation, and the children of Machir son of Manasseh were also placed at birth on Joseph's knees.

versions.text: and saw the third generation of Ephraim's children. The children of Machir son of Manasseh were also placed at birth on Joseph's knees.
versions.explanation: Beginning the verse with "and saw" leaves it without a subject and dependent on the previous verse. "Ephraim's children to the third generation" also renders בְּנֵי שִׁלֵּשִׁים more clearly than "the third generation of Ephraim's children."

text: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and bring you up out of this land to the land he promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, "God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place."
So Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
